subject: Sentinelle.ai discovery — inference goals & proposed topology
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex@sentinelle.ai>, María López <maria@sentinelle.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Sentinelle.ai discovery — inference goals & proposed topology

Hi Alex / María —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we all have the same baseline and clear next steps. I kept this intentionally short; Karthik and I also captured a tentative topology sketch attached.

Top-line goals / pain:
- Replace current self-hosted CPU-based inference for intent classification and agent assist workflows — latency currently 600-800ms p95 and cost spike under load.
- SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for 99% of requests during normal traffic; burst tolerance to 300ms for short windows.
- Throughput need: steady 150–200 QPS for short (2–4 token output) classification calls plus intermittent 40–60 QPS multi-turn assistant sessions with larger context.
- Model constraints: instruction-following, ~8k context preferred, must support constrained output formats (JSON templates) for downstream systems.

Suggested Redwood approach (high level):
- Deployment: Dedicated pool in us-west with fallback to hosted multi-tenant model pool in another region for failover.
- Model variants: for latency-sensitive classification use a quantized 4-bit variant; for assistant use full-precision/FP16 variant on higher-memory GPUs.
- Caching: aggressive KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts and short classification prefix templates.
- Batching: continuous batching windows tuned for 5–12ms aggregation to keep latency SLO.

Attachments I’m including: sentinelle-prod-load-sample.csv (sample traffic slices), initial-multipage-map.pdf (topology + notes).

Asks / agreed next steps:
1) Alex — share a 48-hour sample of request/response logs (anonymized) and typical token sizes (avg input/output). If you can’t share logs, the CSV will help.
2) Karthik & team — schedule a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with Sentinelle engineers to validate the topology, exact GPU SKU recommendations, and quantization trade-offs. Proposed slots below.
3) I’ll put together a 2-week pilot proposal (scope, success criteria, cost estimate) once we have request-size and concurrency numbers.

Proposed deep-dive windows (PST):
- Tue Mar 16: 10:00–11:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Wed Mar 17: 09:00–10:30

Thanks — appreciate the candid discussion today.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the tidy recap. Confirming a few items and adding context:

- We can provide a 72-hour anonymized request log by EOD Monday. Typical request sizes: classification calls average ~45 tokens in, ~6 tokens out; assistant sessions average ~320 tokens in, ~280 tokens out across turns.
- Peak concurrency historically during daytime cresting at ~260 concurrent requests for short calls. We believe 200 QPS steady is conservative.
- Security: Sentinelle is SOC2 Type II in progress; we’ll need to review Redwood’s data handling and audit log retention (please include that in the pilot doc). I’m attaching our security questionnaire PDF — several items are high-priority for procurement.

Pilot ask: we prefer a two-week pilot with production-ish traffic routed to a dedicated pool (shadow or small % rollout). Success criteria: meet p95 <= 150ms for classification at 200 QPS and no significant error spike for assistant sessions. Also need an estimate for expected monthly spend at pilot scale.

I’m happy to take Tue Mar 16 10:00 PST.

—Alex
Alex Grant, CTO
Sentinelle.ai
alex@sentinelle.ai

Subject: Re: Sentinelle.ai discovery — inference goals & proposed topology

Alex / Vanessa —

Appreciate the logfile commitment, Alex. A few technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive so we can tailor the architecture review:

1) Token distribution: your avg/peak numbers are very helpful. For estimations we’ll assume 45 tokens in / 6 out for classification, 320/280 for assistant. Please confirm 99th percentile output sizes for assistant sessions (helps sizing KV cache and sequence-length planning).

2) Concurrency vs QPS: is the 260 concurrent figure an instantaneous spike or sustained over minutes? If spikes are very brief, we can recommend burst autoscaling windows.

3) SLA & retention: what audit/log retention window does procurement require (30/90/365 days)? That will affect our hosted fallback and logging export cadence.

Preliminary topology notes (attached YAML):
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-80GB equiv (split across two availability zones) with a small warm pool (1–2 instances) for fast autoscale.
- Multi-tier model routing: classifier -> quantized small-model endpoints; assistant -> FP16 larger-model endpoints.
- Fallback: cross-region hosted endpoints with async queuing for non-blocking requests during failover.
- Observability hooks: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95 traces wired into your Sentry/Datadog.

I attached a draft 'redwood-deploy-topology-draft.yaml' to illustrate the resource split and routing policies — this is a starting point for the deep-dive. For the pilot cost estimate I’ll run a quick cost model using the token distributions and concurrency patterns once we have the 72-hour log.

See you Tue 10:00 PST.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
